verses.1: And Joshua received much honor and wealth. He was given them by Ahau’av.
verses.2: And he went down to Akhavah for two years, to serve there. Akhavah gave him sheep and grain in abundance, as well as food for his people. He also encouraged him to go up to Ramot Gilad.
verses.3: And Ahaziah, king of Israel, said to Jehoash, king of Judah, “Go with me to Ramoth Gilead.” He replied, “As I am with you, so will I be with you. Your people and mine shall fight together in battle.”
verses.4: And Joshua said to the king of Israel, “Please hear what the LORD has said today.”
verses.5: And the king of Israel took four thousand soldiers. He said to them, “Go to Gilgal and prepare for battle. If you fail, then God will be with the king.” They replied, “Let us go, and God will be with the king.”
verses.6: And Josaphat said, “Is there no more prophet of Jehovah? It is necessary to seek one from among them.”
verses.7: And the king of Israel said to Joshua, “Let there be one man chosen by me to serve as priest to Jehovah. I like him because he is not subject to me in any way. All his days were filled with evil deeds. He was a wicked man.” Then Joshua said, “Do not say, ‘The king says so.’”
verses.8: And the king of Israel called one of Saris’ men and said, “Quickly, bring Mikhael son of Imleah.”
verses.9: And the kings of Israel and Judah sit on their thrones, wearing crowns of jewels. They sit in the court of the gate of Zion. And all the prophets are brought before them.
verses.10: And Tzidkiah of Canaan made iron horns for him. He said, “As the Lord has said, ‘I will destroy the land of Aram until it is completely destroyed.’”
verses.11: And all the prophets were sent forth in this manner: “Go up to Gilgal, and succeed in your mission. Then Jehovah will give the king what he needs.”
verses.12: And the angel who went to call Micah said to him, “Look! The words of the prophets are one good thing. Please let your word be like one of them.” And you said something good.
verses.13: And Michiah said, “May the LORD live! For what God has said, I will speak.”
verses.14: And he went before the king. The king said to him, “Michah, go to Ramot Gilad for battle. If you succeed, then we will give you your request.”
verses.15: And the king said to him, “How many times must I repeat to you that you must speak only the truth in the name of Jehovah?”
verses.16: And he said, “I saw all of Israel flying around on the mountains like sheep without any shepherd. Then God said, ‘Do not let these people return to their homes in peace.’”
verses.17: And the king of Israel said to Joshua, “Have you not told me that I should not receive any good from you, except for evil?”
verses.18: And he said to them, “Hear the word of the LORD. I saw the LORD sitting on His throne, and all the armies in heaven stood around Him.”
verses.19: And the LORD said, “Who will make Ahazib king of Israel happy? He will rise and fall in great distress. And He said, “This is one way; this is another way.”
verses.20: And the wind arose, and stood before Jehovah. It said, “I am afraid.” Then Jehovah said to it, “In the morning.”
verses.21: And he said, “I will go away, and I will become a false spirit among all his prophets.” And he said, “You shall speak lies, and you shall also do what he commands you to do.”
verses.22: And now, behold, Jehovah has given false words from the mouths of your prophets. And Jehovah has spoken evil against you.
verses.23: And Zidkiah son of Kanana went and struck Michaiah on the face. Then he said, “Is this the path that the Spirit of God has chosen for me to speak with you?”
verses.24: And Michai said, “You see that day when you will enter a house to take shelter.”
verses.25: And the king of Israel said, “Take Micah and return him to Amnon, the governor of the city, and to Joash, the son of the king.”
verses.26: And you said, “Thus said the king: ‘Let this house be destroyed, and let its contents be turned into bread and water for sustenance, until I return in peace.’”
verses.27: And Michai said, “If you return in peace, then the LORD will not speak against me.” But he said, “Let all nations hear this.”
verses.28: And the king of Israel and the king of Judah went up to Ramoth Gilead.
verses.29: And the king of Israel said to Joshua, “Arise and go into battle. You shall be my armor bearer.” So the king of Israel arose and went into battle.
verses.30: And the king of Aram ordered the soldiers who were with him to say, “Do not fight against the small ones or against the strong ones. For only the king of Israel alone should fight.”
verses.31: And it came to pass that the officers of the army saw Joshua. They said, “This is King Joshua! Let us attack him!” But Joshua cried out, “Help me, God!” And God helped him.
verses.32: And it became clear that there would be no king of Israel, and so they turned away from him.
verses.33: And a man rushed forward, trying to get close to the king of Israel. He rushed him between the shields and the armor. Then he said to him, “Turn your hand over, so that I can rescue you from the camp.” For I had begun to act.
verses.34: The battle took place on that day. King Israel was seated in his chariot, from sunrise until noon. He died at the time when the sun rose.
